tldr: AKS can now host Foundry models and agents on clusters you already operate, keeping GPU capacity and platform controls in your hands.
Foundry's model router can be called without a separate deployment, while new agent insights add GA trace analysis for troubleshooting.
For AI infrastructure decisions, Vercel's push to verify providers' zero-data-retention claims and new research on VM isolation are worth watching.

top.title: AKS can run Foundry models and agents on your own clusters
top.summary: AKS AI Manager for Foundry lets teams deploy open-weight models and Foundry-hosted agents on existing AKS clusters. The announcement also cites updates to agent sandboxing, GPU operations, confidential computing, and multi-cluster management.
top.why: Assess whether this lets you host workloads on existing GPU capacity while retaining control of networking, identity, and policy, rather than using a fully managed serving path.

top.title: Foundry model router can be called without a separate deployment
top.summary: In supported regions, a Responses or Chat Completions request can set the model to auto and use the router without deploying it first. Auto uses Balanced routing by default.
top.why: Test whether this simplifies deployment management for workloads that can let Foundry select a model, and check regional support before designing around it.

top.title: Foundry makes required agent guardrails visible in project setup
top.summary: The updated Guardrails experience surfaces administrator-required controls for projects, including classifiers, deterministic rules, and LLM-based judges.
top.why: Review how centrally required safety controls fit your agent deployment workflow, especially where teams need to prove policy compliance.

top.title: Foundry IQ adds an ontology-guided enterprise knowledge graph
top.summary: The preview extracts entities and relationships from unstructured content using an ontology you provide, then makes those relationships available as a Foundry IQ knowledge source.
top.why: Evaluate it for questions that depend on relationships across documents, rather than assuming ordinary document retrieval will capture those links.

top.title: Agent insights for Microsoft Foundry are generally available
top.summary: Agent insights groups traces into recurring patterns so teams can investigate common failures; agent optimizer can then test potential fixes.
top.why: Consider this in your production observability plan: it may help teams prioritize repeated agent failures instead of inspecting traces one by one.

also.title: Foundry IQ's iterative retriever can search again for complex questions
also.summary: IQ Retriever Zero can break a question into focused searches, review results, and search again within a configured budget before passing evidence to the answering model.

also.title: Foundry IQ can index uploaded files without a separate storage account
also.summary: The generally available Files knowledge source processes and indexes uploaded files for retrieval without requiring you to provision a storage account or scheduled indexer.

also.title: Foundry previews human annotation for agent evaluations
also.summary: Reviewers can add ratings, tags, comments, and expected outputs to agent traces, then use the annotated conversations to build evaluations.

also.title: Logic Apps Standard adds a built-in MSMQ connector
also.summary: The connector lets Logic Apps Standard workflows interact with existing MSMQ queues, providing a migration bridge for systems that cannot yet replace that messaging technology.

also.title: Azure DevOps previews agentic autofix for Advanced Security alerts
also.summary: The preview uses agents to help fix GitHub Advanced Security alerts in Azure DevOps, with expanded alert coverage and improved failure handling.

top.title: Amazon is acquiring Decart's AI technology and team in a reported $7.5B deal
top.summary: Amazon plans to acquire AI startup Decart's core technology and hire its technical team; the companies did not disclose terms, but sources cited by Bloomberg put the deal at about $7.5 billion. The acquisition comes as Amazon prepares to sell Trainium chips.
top.why: Track whether Amazon turns the acquired optimization technology into a meaningful Trainium advantage before making long-term assumptions about accelerator choice or cloud portability.

top.title: Swahili speech recognition struggles with code-switching and local slang
top.summary: A March 2026 preprint reported a 3.24% word error rate on prepared Swahili readings from Mozilla Common Voice, but everyday Kenyan speech mixes Swahili and English with local Sheng slang, a harder test for recognition systems.
top.why: Use representative, code-switched audio in speech-service evaluations; strong benchmark results on prepared speech may not predict performance for your users.

also.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce an open-source Linux runtime for patch protection
also.summary: Shirudo is an open-source runtime designed to help teams protect running Linux systems while they roll out patches.

top.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship agents can review, fix, and approve pull requests
top.summary: Claude Ship introduces agents that handle routine code-review work, make fixes, and approve pull requests. The aim is to reduce the review bottleneck as AI-generated code increases.
top.why: If you pilot it, decide which repositories and changes can be approved automatically and keep human review for changes with production or security impact.

top.title: Vercel says AI providers will need to prove they honor zero data retention
top.summary: Vercel says it will verify providers' zero-data-retention claims for AI Gateway, where developers have been able to request provider-level ZDR since April.
top.why: For sensitive workloads, treat provider data-retention terms as a routing and procurement requirement, and check what evidence supports the claim before sending prompts.

top.title: CNCF research finds VMs still host 53% of production applications
top.summary: CNCF and Linux Foundation Research report that virtual machines host an average of 53% of production applications; they also find AI and agent workloads increasing demand for virtualization where stronger execution isolation is needed.
top.why: Keep VM-based isolation in the design options for agents that need tighter boundaries; the research does not support assuming every AI workload belongs in a container.

also.title: Google describes identity and containment patterns for production AI agents
also.summary: At QCon, Google's Amanda Walker described treating agents as insider-risk workloads and outlined identity, credential, and containment patterns for production use.
